title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lansford, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lansford, ND
metaDescription: Lansford sits near Bottineau County's Newburg field, one of the county's original 1950s oil discoveries. See what that means for your family's interest.
heroLead: Lansford is a small Bottineau County town near the historic Newburg field, the discovery that first put this part of North Dakota on the oil map generations before the Bakken shale boom.
intro: Families with a Lansford-area mineral interest often hold a fraction tied to that older Newburg-era production, and because it has run for decades, the paper trail behind it can actually be more complete than for newer Bakken interests further west, once you know where to look.

sections.heading: Lansford and the Original Newburg Discovery
paragraphs: The Newburg field, found in the late 1950s, sits near Lansford and represents one of the earliest producing discoveries in this part of the state, well before horizontal drilling technology existed.

sections.heading: What a Legacy Lansford Interest Typically Looks Like
paragraphs: Production from wells in this area tends to be modest and steady, generating a consistent, if smaller, royalty check compared to the high early-life volumes seen in newer Bakken wells.

sections.heading: Tracing Ownership Back to the Original Patent
paragraphs: The Bottineau County Recorder's office holds deed and probate records that, given the area's long production history, often trace back further than owners expect.

sections.heading: What We Look For Before Making a Lansford Offer
paragraphs: We review documented production history alongside current well status before discussing any number on a Lansford-area interest, since the area's decades-long Newburg-era production history gives us a more complete picture than a single recent statement would.

faqs.question: Is Lansford close to the historic Newburg field?
faqs.answer: Yes, Lansford sits near the Newburg field, discovered in the late 1950s and among the earliest producing oil discoveries in this part of North Dakota.

faqs.question: Why does my Lansford royalty check stay about the same each month?
faqs.answer: Legacy wells from this era typically produce at steady, modest rates rather than the faster decline of a new horizontal well, which keeps monthly checks fairly consistent.

faqs.question: How far back do Lansford mineral records typically go?
faqs.answer: Given decades of continuous production in this area, records at the Bottineau County Recorder's office often trace back further than in newer development areas.

faqs.question: Is my small Lansford interest worth selling?
faqs.answer: That depends on your own goals. Steady legacy production can be attractive to hold or to sell, and we lay out both options honestly once we've reviewed your record.

faqs.question: Does a long production history make my Lansford interest easier to value?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, a longer track record gives a clearer picture of how a well is likely to continue producing, which supports a more confident offer.
